assign.outcome:
**Docs tier audited at 5 widths (400–3440), before round.** 13 pages: `/framework/`, its six sections' landing pages (`core`, `ext`, `styles`, `ui`, `ux`, `web`—substituted `/web/` since `/framework/web/` from the shared brief does not exist), and one `doc/` page per section. 3520 findings (`strip` 534, `touching` 1493, `padding-fat` 564, `padding-thin` 823, `ratio` 94, `no-growth` 12) in [`findings.json`](/framework/ai/2026-09-05/spacing-audit-c/findings.json). Ten crops of the worst, `shots/before/crop-C-*.jpg`.

**Headline: the `<details>`/`<summary>` ‘Readme’ toggle repeats the owner's exact complaint** — 601.6px wide, 57.8px of content, a 10.4x empty strip, identical on `/framework/`, `core/`, `ext/`, `styles/`, `ui/`, `ux/` at 1280px (![](shots/before/crop-C-206.jpg)). And **12 of 13 pages barely grow with the viewport** (median sibling gap 3440÷1280 ≈ 1.2x, against a 2.69x viewport growth) — the docs tier's prose spacing is effectively fixed regardless of screen width.

Reusable script: `C:/Users/mike/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Code-lew42-monorepo/e938046a-4711-446c-9b36-6713cd4e869f/scratchpad/spacing-audit-c.mjs` (takes the round as its one argument, unchanged for the after run).

**Left open:** which `doc/` page ‘counts’ as each section's first for `core`/`ext`/`styles` is a judgment call — those three sections aren't `Doc`-type pages themselves (no Docs tab of their own), so I picked the first `Doc`-type descendant on each section's own recommended reading path. Fixing nothing — evidence only, per brief.
